topicName: Software Composition Analysis (SCA) and Vulnerability Scanning (Snyk, Trivy)
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Software Composition Analysis (SCA) and Vulnerability Scanning in CI/CD"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Modern application development heavily relies on open-source libraries and third-party dependencies. While this accelerates delivery, it also introduces supply chain security risks. Software Composition Analysis (SCA) automates the detection of known vulnerabilities, license compliance issues, and outdated dependencies in your codebase. Integrating SCA tools like Snyk and Trivy into your CI/CD pipeline ensures that security checks occur continuously before code reaches production."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites and Setup"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"A working CI/CD pipeline (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or Jenkins)."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"A Snyk account and an API token configured as a pipeline secret (SNYK_TOKEN)."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Trivy installed as a CLI tool or used via its official container image/action."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 1: Integrating Snyk for Code and Dependency Scanning"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"Snyk specializes in scanning open-source dependencies, container images, and infrastructure-as-code files. Below is an example of a GitHub Actions workflow integrating Snyk to test project dependencies for vulnerabilities."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"name: Snyk SCA Security Check
on: [push]
jobs:
  snyk-scan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout Code
        uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Run Snyk to check for vulnerabilities
        uses: snyk/actions/node@master
        env:
          SNYK_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SNYK_TOKEN }}
        with:
          args: --severity-threshold=high"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 2: Integrating Trivy for Container and File System Scanning"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Trivy is a comprehensive and fast vulnerability scanner maintained by Aquasecurity. It scans filesystem directories, container images, and Git repositories for vulnerabilities and misconfigurations. Here is how you can use Trivy in your CI/CD pipeline to scan a Docker image."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"name: Trivy Container Scan
on: [push]
jobs:
  trivy-scan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout Code
        uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Build Docker Image
        run: docker build -t my-app:${{ github.sha }} .
      - name: Run Trivy vulnerability scanner
        uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@master
        with:
          image-ref: 'my-app:${{ github.sha }}'
          format: 'table'
          exit-code: '1'
          ignore-unfixed: true
          severity: 'CRITICAL,HIGH'"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for SCA in CI/CD"},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Fail builds selectively: Set exit codes to break the build only on 'CRITICAL' or 'HIGH' severity issues to prevent developer fatigue."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Scan early and often: Run SCA checks during Pull Request creation rather than waiting for the main branch merge."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Automate remediation: Configure tools like Snyk to automatically open Pull Requests when a dependency fix becomes available."},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"By combining Snyk and Trivy within your CI/CD pipeline, you establish a robust security gate that safeguards both application dependencies and container runtimes against evolving threats."}]
